news.title: Mumbai: BMC’s move to hand over Bandra Reclamation plots to SRA project’s developer sparks controversy
news.para: A proposal by BMC to hand over public plots in Bandra Reclamation to a private developer has raised concerns. Citizens and public representatives are questioning the necessity of this move. Corporator Karen D’Mello has urged the cancellation of the proposal, citing public access issues. Former corporator Asif Zakaria has challenged the legality of BMC's actions regarding open spaces.

news.title: Kolkata: 100 real estate projects stuck as approvals stall in growth belt of Salt Lake-Sector V-New Town
news.para: The approval process for real estate developments in Bidhannagar Municipal Corporation, New Town Kolkata Development Authority, and Nabadiganta Industrial Township Authority has hit a standstill. Nearly 100 projects, totaling 15 million square feet and involving an investment of around Rs 7,500 crore, are currently stalled, causing difficulties for developers as well as workers, contractors, and related businesses.

news.title: Now, promoters’ track record on Gujarat RERA portal
news.para: The Gujarat Real Estate Regulatory Authority has launched an innovative section on its website specifically designed for homebuyers. This new feature showcases the past performances of project promoters in Gujarat, allowing users to easily access crucial information such as project documents, timelines for completion, and any complaints associated with previous projects.

news.title: Telangana RERA gives ELV Projects six months to finish work on Adibatla flats
news.para: The Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority has mandated that ELV Projects rectify outstanding amenities within six months. Residents of ELV Cosmopolis have raised concerns over frequent power outages and insufficient water supply despite their hefty payments. RERA has directed the developer to guarantee steady electricity and complete essential facilities. Complaints regarding hostel operations in certain apartments fell outside the authority's scope. Failure to comply will incur penalties for ELV Projects.

news.title: Telangana RERA fines Aliens Developers ₹2 crore for collecting 38% of flat price without sale agreement
news.para: The Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority has imposed a hefty fine of ₹2 crore on Aliens Developers for breaching sale agreement regulations. Buyers paid significant amounts without receiving a registered sale agreement. Additionally, Aliens Developers must refund ₹42 lakh to affected buyers and pay interest if they decide to cancel.

news.title: No allotment letter, no builder-buyer agreement: Czar Buildwell ordered to refund ₹1.35 lakh with interest
news.para: Czar Buildwell Pvt Ltd acknowledged that a homebuyer had not received an allotment letter or builder-buyer agreement. After she withdrew from the affordable housing project, her refund was not processed, leading to a consumer commission complaint. The commission ruled that the developer was guilty of severe deficiency in service for failing to refund the money. They ordered the builder to return Rs 1.35 lakh with interest and compensation.

news.title: Bombay HC stays arbitral award against MMRDA and in favour of Lodha in Wadala project
news.para: Bombay high court provided a conditional stay on an arbitration award for Rs 238 crore. The award mandated MMRDA to compensate Lodha Developers for losses from reduced built-up area. MMRDA is required to deposit Rs 145 crore within six weeks for the stay to remain effective. The dispute arose over height permissions for a commercial project in Wadala Truck Terminal.

news.title: Goa opens door to FAR up to 300 and 40-metre buildings, offers regularisation of FAR granted earlier
news.para: Goa's town and country planning department has announced new regulations for additional floor area ratio and building heights. These regulations will apply to plots of 300 square meters and above, allowing for greater development potential. Additionally, existing proposals with granted additional FAR will be regularised under the new rules. The specifics of the fee structure for additional FAR will be determined separately.

news.title: CBI conducts searches at premises of Star Housing Finance's ex-directors
news.para: The CBI has launched searches across six sites linked to the directors of Star Housing Finance Ltd. This action follows a complaint from the National Housing Bank detailing grave allegations of bank fraud. Investigators are looking into claims of fund misappropriation via phony loans, which caused notable financial damage. During the searches, crucial documents and pertinent materials were seized.

news.title: Aroundtown CEO Bar-Hen to step down, two co-CEOs named
news.para: Aroundtown, a significant German real estate company, will witness CEO Barak Bar-Hen stepping down in 2026. Following his departure, Jonas Tintelnot and Kamaldeep Manaktala will assume co-CEO roles. The company reported a notable 62% decline in net profit for the first nine months of the year. Funds from operations decreased as finance expenses increased and one-off gains declined. Additionally, Aroundtown has raised its bottom guidance for future operating performance measurements.

news.title: Pritam Chakraborty, mother sell Mumbai apartment for ₹2.30 crore
news.para: Pritam Chakraborty, renowned singer and music producer, alongside his mother, has sold their apartment in Serenity Shree Sai Wing G.H.I. Co-operative Housing Society located in Andheri West, Mumbai. The property, approximately 980.26 square feet in size, fetched ₹2.30 crore, with registration documents affirming the sale occurred in November 2026. The stamp duty amounted to ₹11.50 lakh, and registration charges were ₹30,000.

news.title: Strata invests ₹250 crore in multi-asset real estate platform Reserve
news.para: Strata plans to invest ₹250 crore in Reserve, a real estate platform, in the third quarter of FY27. Reserve aims to develop assets in various sectors, estimating a gross development value of ₹1,500 crore. The company plans to manage 8-10 projects over the next 12-24 months, primarily focused in Bengaluru. Reserve will also continue to develop its existing residential projects independently.

news.title: India office occupancy may touch 89.5% by March 2028: Report
news.para: India's office market is projected to see occupancy levels rise to 89-89.5% by March 2028. Notably, net office absorption is expected to reach around 62-64 million square feet annually during this period. Demand from Global Capability Centres will contribute 45-50% of this absorption, reflecting a shift towards higher-value functions. Vacancy rates are anticipated to decline in five major markets, enhancing overall performance.

news.title: Residents in Kochi plan protest over water woes
news.para: Residents of Kochi are grappling with severe drinking water shortages, sparking protests in multiple neighborhoods. The challenges arise from a combination of leaks, aging pipelines, and insufficient infrastructure. Areas like Poonithura, Kumbalam, and Fort Kochi are particularly hard-hit. Local councillors have raised concerns, demanding that the Kerala Water Authority take urgent action. Plans for a new water treatment plant could potentially alleviate the ongoing crisis.

news.title: Ten spots in Gurugram to get temporary C&D waste storage facilities: Haryana CM
news.para: Gurgaon is embarking on a significant initiative by establishing ten temporary storage sites dedicated to managing construction and demolition waste effectively. Each planned site spans one hectare and will be fortified to prevent any debris spillage. Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini underscored the urgency for a systematic approach to waste management during a recent meeting.

news.title: SC disposes of building violation pleas; hoteliers in Mussoorie hope for relief
news.para: Recently, over 200 hotels and homestays in Mussoorie were served notices from the Mussoorie Dehradun Development Authority. Following the Supreme Court's decision on unlawful constructions and the misuse of residential zones, those affected can now seek assistance from local authorities. This brings a mixture of hope and concern for hoteliers as regulatory challenges persist, while municipal officials face criticism for inadequate enforcement of existing building rules.

news.title: WSB Real Estate Partners exits six housing investments with 19-21% average IRR
news.para: WSB Real Estate Partners has exited six residential investments across major Indian markets including Bengaluru, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, and the National Capital Region. With an impressive average internal rate of return ranging from 19% to 21%, these exits yielded returns at 1.4 times the initial investment. Notably, these transactions were completed ahead of the planned schedules set for April to November 2026.

news.title: Property dues hit ₹4,740 crore, MCG to issue notices to 1,000 tax defaulters in Gurugram
news.para: MCG plans to recover Rs 4,740 crore in property tax from its biggest 1,000 defaulters. Notices will soon be sent out as part of an extensive recovery campaign, leading to property sealings for those who remain unpaid. MCG is also focusing on improving citizen engagement, ensuring respectful service and prompt attention to issues, while reinforcing the need for strict actions against negligent staff.

news.title: DLF starts to remove diesel generator sets from green spaces in Gurugram
news.para: DLF City management has begun removing unauthorized diesel generator sets from various spots in DLF-1, responding to a compliance notice from the department of town and country planning. Tensions arose as residents challenged the DLF staff's authority during the process. With the National Green Tribunal highlighting generator placement regulations, future hearings are planned to ensure adherence to these guidelines.

news.title: Odisha proposes allowing more commercial use in residential areas
news.para: The Odisha government is set to revise urban planning laws, aiming to boost commercial ventures within residential areas. This proposed shift will affect development zones like Bhubaneswar and Cuttack. New guidelines will allow restricted construction on lands earmarked for future roadways. These changes aim to harmonize the interests of landowners with the needs of local residents. Feedback from stakeholders is encouraged prior to the adoption of the finalized regulations.
